runtime_status: runtime-evidenced on Windows PowerShell 5.1: every MCP server in three live provider configs completed a real initialize -> tools/list exchange, and the three dead command paths found there were repaired and re-verified. Linux/static/artifact gates pass in CI.
notes: v7.9.7: make agents seek the cheapest decisive evidence before guessing, and require real evidence before claiming visual or behavioural work is finished. One new skill, visual-verification, added only after auditing the eleven existing reliability skills confirmed none of them owned appearance -- assumption-audit, research-verification, observability-first, systematic-debugging, verification-before-completion, artifact-proof, real-boundary-testing, tool-output-awareness, source-of-truth, process-lifecycle-cleanup and secret-hygiene were extended at their own seams instead of being cloned. It ships a falsifiable check rather than an instruction: TOOLS/vision-canary is an image whose contents are recorded only as a SHA-256, and TOOLS/Test-VisionCanary.ps1 answers PASS or FAIL, because 'a screenshot was captured' and 'the agent inspected the pixels' are different claims and the honest report and the fabricated one are otherwise the same sentence. Provider vision was established by running each CLI: Claude Code reads image files directly (verified in session), codex and codex exec accept -i/--image (verified in --help; end-to-end untested, the account hit its usage limit), and grok 1.0.5, kimi-code and hermes showed no image-attach flag. TESTS/evidence-scenarios ships eight fixtures for the behaviour itself -- a rendered defect invisible in source, a grey box that is a 404 rather than a CSS bug, a crash whose log already names the cause, the same crash with nothing to read, a version-specific fact the installed binary settles, a stable fact that must NOT trigger research, a screenshot without vision, and proving a secret is set without printing it -- each with a rubric, plus check_fixtures.py chained into the pack gate so the fixtures cannot quietly be repaired into passing everything. Scenario A was run for real: the rendered page shows its heading clipped behind a fixed header, which no DOM or CSS inspection reports. Cleanup the owner asked for: Supabase withdrawn (the only profile needing an account and a token, against this pack's free/local/keyless default) with a migration that un-registers only what this pack recorded and leaves an independently configured server alone; blender-mcp pinned to 1.8.3 against PyPI and discovered from %APPDATA%\Blender Foundation, which the maintainer's own S:\Steam path could never do on another machine -- a release contract now fails the build on any drive letter or user directory in a shipped config. Blender telemetry was read from the 1.8.3 wheel rather than assumed: consent-gated inside the addon, no telemetry endpoint, unreachable from outside the editor, so the note states that instead of claiming a disable. sequential-thinking lost its always-on slot on measurement: real MCP initialize -> tools/list gives 1 tool but a 4,587-byte schema, ~1,146 tokens on every turn of every session, as much as context7's two tools, for a structured scratchpad rather than a capability. It became an opt-in profile with no detection markers instead of being deleted, and machines that already have it are told with the number rather than edited. Godot was re-compared: hi-godot/godot-ai is fresher but needs an editor plugin, uv and a WebSocket, so Coding-Solo's headless npx server is kept and the comparison recorded. A real Codex run exposed a finding this pack had never checked -- 'Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed and 23 additional skills were not included' -- so description-based routing, the pack's whole mechanism, is degraded on Codex at 215 installed skills / 38,228 characters; skill_search is already stable and enabled there, so the installed-state doctor now reports the measured size and the remedy rather than letting it fail silently. 145 canonical skills across 5 provider trees. The always-on preamble grew by one clause, measured: +91 bytes, about 23 tokens per request.
